standard_prerequisites.name: The composite of two universal homeomorphisms is a universal homeomorphism, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Disposes of the case in which the two factors are universal homeomorphisms.

standard_prerequisites.name: A homeomorphism is an affine morphism, and an affine morphism is separated, both cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the auxiliary morphism in the last case is a closed immersion.

standard_prerequisites.name: A section of a morphism of schemes is an immersion, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the identity relation between the auxiliary morphism and the homeomorphism into closedness of the auxiliary morphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of universal homeomorphisms, used here to conclude from bijectivity plus being a closed immersion
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the final conclusion in the last case.

core_obligations: Case of the two factors: if the two morphisms of the composite are universal homeomorphisms, so is the composite, by the cited closure under composition (proof lines 11441-11443).

Case of the composite and the first factor: base change the whole diagram along an arbitrary morphism to the target; the base changed composite and the base changed first factor are homeomorphisms because the class is stable under base change, and a composite is a homeomorphism with one factor a homeomorphism exactly when the other is, so the base changed second factor is a homeomorphism, which is the definition (proof lines 11445-11458).

Case of the composite and the second factor: base change along an arbitrary morphism to the middle scheme, giving a diagram in which an auxiliary morphism from the base change of the middle scheme to a further base change is defined by the universal property of fibre products; the relevant base changed first factor is a homeomorphism by the two-out-of-three property for homeomorphisms, so it suffices to show the auxiliary morphism is a universal homeomorphism (proof lines 11460-11478).

Auxiliary morphism: the base changed second factor is a homeomorphism, hence affine and a fortiori separated, and the auxiliary morphism composed with it is the identity, so the auxiliary morphism is a closed immersion; since the same homeomorphism is bijective, the auxiliary morphism is a bijective closed immersion, hence a universal homeomorphism by the cited characterization (proof lines 11479-11488).
proof_roadmap: Handle the easy case by closure under composition, and the second case by base changing to the target and using the two-out-of-three property for homeomorphisms (proof lines 11441-11458).

In the remaining case, base change to the middle scheme, reduce to an auxiliary morphism defined by the universal property of fibre products, and show it is a bijective closed immersion using affineness and separatedness of the relevant homeomorphism (proof lines 11460-11488).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a morphism presented as a composite of two morphisms, if any two of the three morphisms involved are universal homeomorphisms then so is the third (statement lines 11433-11439). The counted proof treats the three possible pairs: the easy case is closure under composition, the case of the composite and the first factor follows by base changing to the target and using the two-out-of-three property for homeomorphisms, and the remaining case requires base changing to the middle scheme and analysing an auxiliary morphism defined by the universal property of fibre products, which is shown to be a bijective closed immersion because the relevant base changed morphism is a homeomorphism, hence affine and separated (proof lines 11441-11488). It is H2: all three cases are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard closure, affineness and immersion statements.
